newsitem.title: GERMANY: German DAX hits records, then off as profits taken.
newsitem.headline: German DAX hits records, then off as profits taken.

text.p: Germany's DAX index, given energy by a surging U.S. stock market, hit record levels on Tuesday but closed post-bourse electronic dealings somewhat off the day's highs due to profit-taking.

The IBIS DAX, which tracks all-day computer trade in the 30-share DAX index, ended the day up 17.90 points at a record close of 2,718.73 points but was some 15 points below the day's high at 2,734.37.
The DAX earlier closed bourse trade up 34.57 points at 2,728.45 after briefly touching a new high at 2,728.64.
The initial spur for the jump was Wall Street's close on Monday at 6,010 points, the first time the Dow Jones index ended above the crucial 6,000-point level.
A stronger U.S. dollar, which was eyeing 1.54 marks, was also a boost for export-sensitive German firms and gains in German debt markets were also supportive.
"Everything is really positive," said one Frankfurt trader, "It's not just the Dow. People are generally positive on the DAX and we've been consolidating for a few days."

Dealers said the DAX index could advance to 2,750 points later in the week. But others said certain technical indicators meant that the possibility of a sharp downward correction could not be ruled out.
The DAX has spent the last few days consolidating just below the 2,700 level after record highs were posted early last week, but had been widely expected to make another upward run.
Traders said U.S. September consumer price data, scheduled for release at 1230 GMT on Wednesday, would provide the market with further direction.
"The market is very stable. Of course we'll have to see what happens in the U.S. for the rest of the day but most U.S. company figures are coming out well," said one trader.
Dealers said western European car registration figures out after the end of trade on Monday had given a boost to carmaker stocks, which were also boosted by the strength of the dollar.
Car manufacturer Daimler Benz AG was the DAX's biggest climber, ending the IBIS session up 2.12 marks at 86.57 marks, touching a new year's high for IBIS dealings at 86.88 marks.
Auto maker BMW AG also rose, ending IBIS trade up 13.40 marks at 896 marks. BMW announced on Tuesday that its U.K. Rover group was planning to invest in a new vehicle at its Land Rover plant.
